subject: Clarify: marketplace discount stacking and channel margin routing for HealthGrid private offer
messages:
From: Eva Mendes <eva.mendes@healthgrid.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai; procurement@healthgrid.com
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace private offer — discount stacking / partner margin question

Hi Neha,

We're mapping out the HealthGrid private offer for Azure + GCP SKUs and noticed two potential adjustments that affect partner economics: a) a promotional marketplace credit that shows up as a separate line item, and b) the private-offer list discount we're proposing. Our reseller (Valence) is concerned that the promotional credit will be applied post-passback and reduce their effective margin. Can you confirm how Redwood routes discounts and promo credits for marketplace private offers and whether those 'hidden' credits get included in passback calculations?

I've attached a short PRQ with the SKU set and expected volumes. Would appreciate a quick note about the mechanism and any examples you have so we can explain to Valence.

Thanks,
Eva Mendes
Sr. Procurement Manager
HealthGrid
Attachment: HealthGrid_PRQ.xlsx
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Eva Mendes <eva.mendes@healthgrid.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — discount stacking / partner margin question

Hi Eva — thanks for the PRQ. Short answer: promotional credits that originate from the marketplace (platform promotions) are surfaced separately from the private-offer 'list discount' but how they affect partner passback depends on routing and the invoice path.

A few clarifying questions so we give you an accurate example for Valence:
- Is Valence the reseller on the invoice (i.e., will invoices route through their account) or are you buying direct through the marketplace with Valence as an enrolled partner?
- Are the promotional credits time-limited (one-off adoption credits) or recurring (monthly bucket)?

If invoices route via Valence, we typically calculate passback on net-of-list-discounts but prior to marketplace promotional credits. That means partner margin protections should use the negotiated private-offer net, and marketplace promos are treated as post-invoice adjustments (they can reduce net revenue but do not retroactively change the partner entitlement calculation in our standard flow).

I'll loop in Ben from Partner Rev so we can run a short margin workback. If helpful we can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Sales Manager, Marketplace
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai; jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: Eva Mendes <eva.mendes@healthgrid.com>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — discount stacking / partner margin question

Adding the margin workback details we discussed. High level: there are three revenue events to track — private-offer invoiced list discount, marketplace promotional credit, and reseller passback. Our established approach for similar Health sector deals:
- Compute partner entitlement on the invoiced amount after the private-offer discount (so partner gets a share of the contracted net).
- Apply marketplace promotional credits post-invoice reconciliation; these are accounted for separately and do not change historical partner entitlements unless the partner contract explicitly ties passback to net-of-promos.

Concrete example (numbers simplified, monthly):
- List price: $100k
- Private-offer list discount: 30% -> Invoiced: $70k
- Partner passback rate (agreed): 15% -> Partner entitlement: $10.5k
- Marketplace promo credit (one-off adoption): $5k applied after invoicing -> Net revenue after promo: $65k (company receives $65k after promo)
- Under our standard flow, the partner still receives $10.5k unless the contract ties passback to net-after-promo (rare).

If Valence wants margin protection that accounts for promo credits we can bake a clause in the private-offer or create a reserve/escrow to make them whole. I've attached a quick CSV with the workback and two alternative flows: (A) standard (passback from post-discount/invoice), (B) promo-aware (passback adjusted to always meet X% of gross).

Attachment: margin_workback.csv

Hope this helps — happy to run numbers against your PRQ.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Partner Revenue
Redwood Inference
From: Eva Mendes <eva.mendes@healthgrid.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: cloud-partner@valence.io; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 04 May 2028 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — discount stacking / partner margin question

Thanks Ben & Neha — that example is helpful. Valence is the enrolled reseller (they will be listed on the invoice), and their concern is exactly the scenario you outlined: adoption promos are reducing the net post-facto and they want a guarantee.

They've asked for two things: 1) an explicit clause in the private-offer that guarantees a minimum net margin to the reseller (i.e., a floor that triggers a top-up if marketplace credits reduce their effective margin below the agreed level), and 2) a clear timeline for reconciliation and payment of any top-up (quarterly vs. one-off).

Would Redwood be open to a reserve/escrow approach for this account (HealthGrid) for the first 6 months so we can move forward quickly? If so, we need a short MAP (mutual action plan) and a redlineable private-offer PDF to run through procurement.

Regards,
Eva
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Eva Mendes <eva.mendes@healthgrid.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, cloud-partner@valence.io
Date: Mon, 06 May 2028 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — discount stacking / partner margin question

Eva — appreciate the clear ask. Proposal and next steps below:

1) Reserve/escrow pilot: Redwood will agree to a 6-month reserve for HealthGrid to protect Valence's gross margin on invoiced amounts for the initial term. Operationally this will be handled as a quarterly reconciliation: we calculate realized promo impact and top-up any shortfall to the agreed partner entitlement.

2) Contract language: we'll add a short Schedule (Partner Margin Protection) to the private-offer that defines the calculation, measurement period (quarterly), and dispute window (30 days). We will also include a clause that the reserve is a non-precedent pilot limited to this account and term.

3) MAP & timing:
- Today (05/06) — Redwood shares redlineable private-offer PDF and MAP draft (attached).
- 05/08 — Joint call with Valence, HealthGrid procurement, and Redwood ops to confirm reconciliation cadence.
- 05/12 — Finalize private-offer and start DocuSign routing.
